floor-repair/lakewood-ranch.h1: Floor Repair in Lakewood Ranch: Leaks to Builder Tile
floor-repair/lakewood-ranch.lede: A slow appliance leak is the single most common way a Lakewood Ranch floor ends up on our repair schedule, with builder-grade tile close behind.
floor-repair/lakewood-ranch.capsule: Lakewood Ranch's top repair call is warped LVP behind a leaking washer or dishwasher, followed by hollow-sounding builder-grade tile in the community's first-wave villages like Country Club East and Summerfield. A typical plank repair runs about $190 on our hourly rate in 2026; a six-tile hollow-tile reset runs $570-$1,110.
floor-repair/lakewood-ranch.body_html:
The single most common repair call we get from inside Lakewood Ranch is warped or lifted vinyl plank behind a washing machine or dishwasher, the result of a slow supply-line or drain leak that goes unnoticed for weeks because it's tucked behind an appliance nobody moves. By the time the warping is visible along the seam lines, the leak has usually been running long enough to affect the subfloor underneath as well as the plank itself, which is why we check moisture levels a few feet past the visible damage before pricing anything. See our Lakewood Ranch area page for the full village breakdown.

Builder-grade porcelain tile is the second pattern, and it shows up earliest in the community's first-wave villages, homes from the 2006-2012 build-out in Country Club East and Summerfield, where original construction crews working fast through dozens of identical floor plans sometimes skipped full mortar coverage under the tile. A hollow-sounding tile in one of those kitchens usually isn't a sign of a new problem; it's an eighteen-year-old installation shortcut finally showing itself as foot traffic and thermal cycling work the weak bond loose.

Cracked tile that follows a straight line across a room, rather than an isolated tile here and there, points to a different cause entirely: a hairline crack in the slab itself, telegraphing up through the grout joint. That's less common in Lakewood Ranch than in older parts of the county, since the community's slabs are decades newer, but it does happen in a handful of first-generation homes where the original pour had a control-joint gap in the wrong place. We test with an infrared or pin-type moisture meter before deciding whether the fix is a straight tile pull-and-reset or something that needs a crack-isolation membrane installed under the replacement.

A two-story home with an upstairs bathroom leak that's found its way to a ceiling or floor below is the other repeat call, treated as urgent regardless of which village it's in, since drywall and subfloor damage compound quickly the longer standing water sits.
floor-repair/lakewood-ranch.cost_html:
A typical warped-plank repair behind a washing machine: four affected LVP planks plus the section of subfloor that absorbed the leak. Plank-level repairs price on our $95 hourly rate since LVP swap-outs aren't a fixed per-unit charge; a typical two-hour repair runs about $190, and the $185 diagnostic fee counts toward that total rather than adding to it.

A hollow-tile reset in a Country Club East or Summerfield kitchen, six tiles along the affected run, runs $95-$185 per tile ($570-$1,110), plus regrouting the repaired area at $3.50-$7.00 per sq ft if the surrounding grout doesn't match cleanly. Check the floor repair cost guide for pricing on every other repair category we handle.

faqs.q: Why is my vinyl plank floor warped near my washing machine in Lakewood Ranch?
faqs.a: A slow supply-line or drain leak behind the appliance is the most common cause we find in the community, and by the time the warping is visible along the seams, the leak has usually been running long enough to affect the subfloor too, which is why we check moisture past the visible damage.

faqs.q: Why does my Country Club East kitchen tile sound hollow?
faqs.a: Homes from Lakewood Ranch's 2006-2012 first wave sometimes have original tile installed with incomplete mortar coverage, a common shortcut on fast-moving new-construction crews, and that shows up eighteen-plus years later as a hollow sound under foot traffic.

faqs.q: Is cracked tile in my Lakewood Ranch home a slab problem?
faqs.a: It can be, though it's less common here than in older parts of the county since the community's slabs are newer. Cracked tile that follows a straight line usually means a hairline slab crack is telegraphing through the grout joint, and we test for that before repricing the repair.
